ticket.title: miter contracts prints 32 field-level drift lines and still exits 0
ticket.description:
Measured while verifying GB-221: `miter contracts` output ends with 32 lines of the form "<entity> <field> in [rust] but missing in [typescript]" (typed_hole, workspace_capabilities and others) and the process exits 0, so the Tier 3 gate step passes while drift is visible in its own output. A gate that reports a problem and returns success is not a gate - it is the same failure mode as GB-202 before GB-219 wired it in, and as the outfeed gate accepting a skipped step as a pass.

The 32 lines are pre-existing, not from GB-221: a targeted grep for reasoning in the same run returns 0 hits, so the ReasoningEffort change is contract-clean.

TWO THINGS TO DECIDE: (1) should field-level drift fail the run, or only entity-level? Some drift may be expected where a language legitimately lacks a field, in which case it needs the same allowlist treatment GB-202 gave lateral edges - an entry with a ticket, not silence. (2) 35 entities verified versus 32 drift lines suggests the comparison is per-field across 3 languages and will need a stated policy rather than an implicit one.

completed_items: Fixed in two commits. 3648091 miter-cli: added --check, extracted the verdict from the two renderers, 3 unit tests (drift without check describes, drift with check rejects, clean passes, singular not pluralised); also re-exported MissingFieldDrift which was public shape but unreachable by name. b851188 outfeed-core: the gate contracts step now passes --check. Verified against the installed binary: plain `miter contracts` exits 0 with the report, `--check` exits 1 with "contract drift: 9 entities across 33 field(s)".
remaining_items: The gate is now honest and red, which is the point. GB-238 holds the work: 9 entities, 33 fields, and a design question - the checker matches on entity name, so some pairs are genuinely one drifted wire contract (benchwork ChatMessage: content/timestamp_ms vs text/timestamp) while others merely share a name between a Rust ledger record and a TypeScript UI model. Deciding which is which has to come before any field is renamed.
handoff.last_error_or_blocker: None. Note the field count moved 32 -> 33 between filing and fixing: the first count was taken against a three-day-stale index (GB-237), so the stale index was hiding a drift as well as symbols.
